about: Small graphs for max-cut, each with its maximum cut found by exhaustive search over every split (node n−1 fixed, so each split is counted once). 'optimal_splits' is how many splits reach it.

graphs.name: Petersen graph
graphs.about: A famous small graph: 10 nodes, each with 3 neighbours, and no short cycles. It has an odd cycle, so not every edge can be cut.

graphs.name: 20 nodes, 3 neighbours each
graphs.about: A random 3-regular graph (seed 7): a common test problem for quantum optimisation methods.

graphs.name: 22 nodes, random links
graphs.about: Each pair linked with probability 0.25 (seed 3): uneven degrees, many odd cycles.

graphs.name: A 4 × 6 grid
graphs.about: A check: a grid is two-colourable like a chessboard, so the best split cuts every edge.
